input.risks:
1. Type edit is semantically a no-op for TS (`'auto'` is already a valid `ColorString`), so it cannot be validated by the compiler; the real behavior lives entirely in GaugeView.ts. Do not "fix" this by intersecting `ItemStyleOption & { color?: ColorString | 'auto' }` — that collapses `color` to `string` and silently removes gradient/pattern support from `progress.itemStyle.color`.
2. Emphasis/blur/select states are NOT covered: `setStatesStylesFromModel(progress, itemModel)` (GaugeView.ts:568) reads `emphasis.itemStyle` (default styleType 'itemStyle', src/util/states.ts:812-819), not `emphasis.progress.itemStyle`, so `'auto'` inside a state block would leak through as the literal string 'auto'. The pointer has the identical limitation, so this is pre-existing and arguably out of scope — but if a reviewer asks, that is the answer.
3. Series-level `itemStyle.color: 'auto'` is a different mechanism: src/visual/style.ts:92-111 rewrites `globalStyle.fill/stroke === 'auto'` to the palette color before the view runs. So `series.itemStyle.color: 'auto'` means "palette", while the new `series.progress.itemStyle.color: 'auto'` means "axisLine stop color". Same keyword, two meanings — matching the existing pointer/splitLine/axisTick semantics, but worth a doc line.
4. NaN / out-of-range values: `linearMap(NaN, ...)` yields NaN and `getColor(NaN)` falls through the loop to the last stop, i.e. `colorList[colorList.length - 1][1]`. Identical to the current pointer behavior; no new guard added.
5. `getColor` closes over `colorList` from `axisLine.lineStyle.color` even when `axisLine.show` is false, so `'auto'` still resolves against the (possibly single-stop) default `[[1, tokens.color.neutral10]]` (GaugeSeries.ts:222). With the default single grey stop, `progress.itemStyle.color: 'auto'` renders grey — expected, not a bug.
6. Ordering inside the block matters: the `'auto'` check must come AFTER `progress.setStyle(itemModel.getModel(['progress', 'itemStyle']).getItemStyle())` (otherwise the option value has not landed on the element yet) and before/after `setStatesStylesFromModel` is irrelevant.
